bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where reading from invalid memory occurs if there are fewer capturing parentheses than the available space in the external ovector.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` with a `READ of size 496` in `match` at `src/pcre2_match.c:819` while the staged 8-byte PoC `(R?){65}` ran through `pcre2_fuzzer`. The harness compiles those same bytes twice: first with input-derived `compile_options`, then with `compile_options = PCRE2_NEVER_BACKSLASH_C` on the second loop iteration, and the saved crash artifacts do not identify which pass reached the crashing `pcre2_match()` call. What the staged source does prove for this exact witness is that it contains only one explicit parenthesized atom, so any compiled pattern in the crashing run can contribute at most one capturing group and therefore reaches matching with `re->top_bracket <= 1`. Independently, the harness allocates `match_data` with `pcre2_match_data_create(32, NULL)`, so the external ovector always has 32 pairs. The crash occurs in `match()`'s success epilogue at `memcpy(ovector+2, Fovector, (oveccount - 1) * 2 * sizeof(PCRE2_SIZE));`, which uses the external `oveccount` alone and copies 31 capture pairs, i.e. the recorded 496-byte read, from the current frame's internal `Fovector` before the next line clamps with `min(top_bracket + 1, oveccount)`. With `top_bracket <= 1`, the internal frame carries data for at most one captured group, so this over-reads the stack-resident `stack_frames_vector`, matching the saved ASan report. The fix computes the minimum first and copies only the actually present internal entries.

source.description: When `parse_regex` handles the witness's only explicit `(`, it either increments `cb->bracount` once or emits `META_NOCAPTURE` depending on `PCRE2_NO_AUTO_CAPTURE`. This is the first project-code site that materializes the small capture-count state later stored in `re->top_bracket`.
source.value_from: The staged 8-byte PoC is ASCII `(R?){65}`. It contains exactly one parenthesized atom around `R?` and no other parentheses, so this parser site can materialize at most one capturing group on any compile pass.

sink.description: ASan crash site. This `memcpy` reads the recorded 496 bytes from the current frame's internal `Fovector` even though the crashing compiled pattern from this witness can expose at most one captured-group pair there, so the read runs off the stack-resident `stack_frames_vector`.

root_cause.description: The result-copy length is derived only from the external `oveccount`, so the harness-fixed 32-pair ovector makes `match()` copy 31 capture pairs before it consults `top_bracket + 1`. For this witness the crashing compiled pattern has `top_bracket <= 1`, so the internal frame provides at most one capture pair and the copy over-reads it. The fix first clamps with `min(top_bracket + 1, oveccount)` before calling `memcpy`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness forwards the exact staged witness bytes into the PCRE2 compiler. Compilation succeeds in the reproduced run because execution later reaches `pcre2_match_8` and the crashing `match()` epilogue.

tainted_value_origin.description: Harness boundary that forwards the exact 8-byte PoC into `pcre2_compile()` as the pattern on both compile passes; the crashing `code` object is compiled from those same bytes.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` file has SHA-256 `356ad77b944665a3190ad13ab30520d51e0687d111bd1f43da780e1e1b69d4e0` and exact ASCII contents `(R?){65}`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness compiles the exact witness in two passes, allocates `match_data` once with a fixed 32-pair external ovector after the first successful compile, and then matches the same bytes as the subject.
Parsing the witness's only explicit parenthesized atom yields a compiled pattern with `re->top_bracket <= 1`, regardless of which compile pass later reaches the crash.
Internal frame-ovector state is derived from `re->top_bracket`, but `match()` is invoked with the harness-fixed external `match_data->oveccount = 32`.
On the successful `OP_END` path, the vulnerable epilogue copies `(oveccount - 1) * 2` slots from `Fovector` before clamping to `top_bracket + 1`, producing the reproduced 496-byte stack over-read.

fine_trace.note: Harness boundary. The exact PoC bytes `(R?){65}` are compiled in a two-pass loop: first with input-derived `compile_options`, then with `compile_options = PCRE2_NEVER_BACKSLASH_C` on the second iteration. The saved crash stack at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:193` does not identify which compile pass reached the sink, so downstream steps use only branch-insensitive facts shared by any crashing compile of this witness.

Source. When the parser reaches the witness's only explicit `(`, this site either increments `cb->bracount` and emits `META_CAPTURE | 1` or, if `PCRE2_NO_AUTO_CAPTURE` is set on that compile pass, emits `META_NOCAPTURE`. Because the PoC contains no other parentheses, this project-code consumption of the input establishes `cb->bracount <= 1` for any compiled pattern that can later crash.

The compiled regex stores the parser count directly. For this exact witness, the crash-causing `code` object can therefore reach matching with `re->top_bracket` equal to either 0 or 1, but never larger.

On the first successful compile, the harness allocates `match_data` with a fixed external ovector capacity of 32 pairs and then reuses it for later matches. The crashing `pcre2_match()` call therefore sees `match_data->oveccount = 32` regardless of which compile pass produced `code`.

Internal frame setup is derived from `re->top_bracket`, and only `re->top_bracket * 2 * sizeof(PCRE2_SIZE)` bytes of capture slots are initialized in the current frame ovector. For this witness that is at most one captured-group pair; ASan later identifies the backing stack object as `stack_frames_vector` in `pcre2_match_8`'s frame.

fine_trace.code:
rc = match(start_match, mb->start_code, match_data->ovector,
  match_data->oveccount, re->top_bracket, frame_size, mb);
fine_trace.note: The main matcher receives the mismatch directly: external `match_data->oveccount = 32` from the harness, but internal frame state derived from `re->top_bracket <= 1`. The saved crash stack proves the reproduced run reaches this call from `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:193`.

Root cause. On the successful `OP_END` path, the copy length uses only external `oveccount`, so the harness-fixed 32-pair ovector requests 31 capture pairs, the recorded 496-byte read, from `Fovector` before the next line computes `i = 2 * ((top_bracket + 1 > oveccount)? oveccount : top_bracket + 1)`. For this witness `top_bracket <= 1`, so the source frame should contribute at most one captured-group pair.

Sink. `memcpy` reads the recorded 496 bytes from the current frame's `Fovector` inside `stack_frames_vector`; ASan reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 496` and identifies `stack_frames_vector` `[368, 10608)` as the overflowed stack object in `pcre2_match_8`'s frame.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executes `pcre2_fuzzer` on the staged `poc` and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 496` in `match`, matching `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt`.

format.name: raw PCRE2 pattern bytes
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 8-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_781/poc` with SHA-256 `356ad77b944665a3190ad13ab30520d51e0687d111bd1f43da780e1e1b69d4e0`; its ASCII contents are exactly `(R?){65}`. The harness compiles this same byte sequence twice and the saved crash artifacts do not identify which compile pass reached the sink, so the staged evidence supports only the branch-insensitive fact that the crashing compiled pattern from this witness has `top_bracket <= 1` while the external `match_data` still has the harness-fixed 32-pair ovector. The saved run proves this exact file reaches the `OP_END` success epilogue at `src/pcre2_match.c:819` and triggers the recorded 496-byte over-read there. The staged evidence does not justify a broader trigger than this exact witness and observed crash path.
